learn.hook: Who opens the school gate before you arrive? Who makes the garden bloom? A school runs because many people work together!
points: A school community is all the people who make the school work: students, teachers, the principal, office staff, cleaning staff, the gardener, the guard, cooks and bus drivers.
Each person's work is important, so we respect and thank everyone.
Parents also help. They meet teachers and may be part of the School Management Committee.
Students help too: as class monitors, in the eco-club, by keeping the classroom clean and caring for the school garden.
A good school welcomes everyone. Ramps help wheelchair users, books in Braille help children who cannot see, and sign language helps children who cannot hear.

example.q: A new girl, Lhamo, uses a wheelchair. Her classroom is on the first floor and there is no ramp or lift. Think it through: what can the school do?
steps: Every child has the right to reach the classroom.
A ramp or lift would help her move on her own.
Until then, the class could be moved to the ground floor.
example.answer: Build a ramp or lift, and meanwhile hold her class on the ground floor.

learn.reallife: Next time you see the school guard, the cleaning didi or bhaiya, or the gardener, say 'Thank you!' They help make your school a happy place.

games.title: Who does what?
pairs: Cares for plants in the school garden

items.text: A sloping path for wheelchairs is called a ___.
Raised dots that let people read with their fingers are called ___.
People who cannot hear may talk using ___ language.
A student who helps the teacher keep the class in order is the class ___.

quiz.q: Which group best describes a school community?
options: Students, teachers, staff and parents together
Only the people who live near the school
quiz.explain: Everyone who helps the school run is part of its community.
steps: A school community is everyone who makes the school work.
It includes students, teachers, staff and parents.
Answer: Students, teachers, staff and parents together
quiz.mistake: Thinks only teachers or students make a school

quiz.q: Who usually looks after the plants in the school garden?
quiz.explain: The gardener (mali) waters, plants and cares for the school garden.
steps: The gardener (mali) cares for the school garden.
Answer: The gardener
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the jobs of school staff

quiz.q: Why should we respect the cleaning staff of our school?
options: They are the oldest people in school
Their work keeps the school clean and healthy for all
quiz.explain: Every job in school is important. A clean school keeps all of us healthy.
steps: Every person's work in school is important.
Cleaning staff keep the school clean and healthy.
Answer: Their work keeps the school clean and healthy for all
quiz.mistake: Thinks only some jobs deserve respect

quiz.q: Braille is a way of reading using
options: raised dots felt with the fingers
quiz.explain: Braille uses patterns of raised dots. People who cannot see read them with their fingertips.
steps: Braille helps children who cannot see.
It uses raised dots felt with the fingers.
Answer: raised dots felt with the fingers
quiz.mistake: Does not know how Braille works

quiz.q: Who invented Braille?
quiz.explain: Louis Braille of France made this reading system. He had lost his own eyesight as a child.
steps: Braille was made by Louis Braille of France.
Answer: Louis Braille
quiz.mistake: Guesses a famous person from a different field

quiz.q: What helps a child who uses a wheelchair enter the school building on their own?
quiz.explain: A ramp is a gentle slope, so a wheelchair can roll up it.
steps: Ramps help wheelchair users.
A gentle slope lets a wheelchair roll up.
Answer: A ramp
quiz.mistake: Does not think about how wheelchairs move

quiz.q: How can students help keep their school a happy place?
options: Keep classrooms clean and be kind to everyone
quiz.explain: Clean, cared-for classrooms and kind friends make school pleasant for all.
steps: Students help by keeping classrooms clean and being kind.
Answer: Keep classrooms clean and be kind to everyone
quiz.mistake: Does not see that students are part of the school community

quiz.q: The School Management Committee includes
quiz.explain: Parents, teachers and local members meet to help plan and improve the school.
steps: Parents meet teachers and may be part of the School Management Committee.
It includes parents, teachers and community members.
Answer: parents, teachers and community members
quiz.mistake: Does not know parents help run schools

teach.ask: Gappu lands on the school gate: 'Is a school just teachers and children? Who else makes it work?'
teach.praise: So many helpers! Teachers, students, staff and parents all work together. I respect them all now!
teach.nudge: Who else, besides teachers and students, works to keep a school running?

revise.summary: A school community is everyone who makes the school work: students, teachers, principal, staff, parents and helpers. Every job matters, and a good school welcomes everyone with ramps, Braille and sign language.
focus: Members of the school community and their jobs
remember: Gardener cares for the garden; cleaning staff keep school healthy
School Management Committee: parents, teachers, community members
Braille: raised dots read with fingers, made by Louis Braille
Ramps for wheelchair users; sign language for children who cannot hear
traps: The school community is not only students or only the principal.
A tall staircase does not help a wheelchair user; a ramp does.

learn.hook: Have you ever felt happy, nervous and excited all on the same day? Feelings are normal, and a happy school helps everyone feel safe.
points: Everyone has feelings: happy, sad, angry, scared or excited. All feelings are okay. Talking about them helps.
When we feel upset, we can take deep breaths, count to ten, or talk to a friend, parent or teacher.
Being kind means sharing, helping, listening and including others in games.
Bullying means hurting someone again and again with words or actions. It is never okay. Tell a teacher or a trusted adult.
Our body is our own. If any touch makes you feel uncomfortable, say 'No', move away, and tell a trusted adult.

example.q: At lunch, Samar sees some children laughing at a new boy's accent every day. Think it through: what should Samar do?
steps: Laughing at someone again and again is bullying.
Samar can be kind to the new boy and sit with him.
He should tell the class teacher so that the bullying stops.
example.answer: Be kind to the new boy and tell a teacher about the bullying.

learn.reallife: Many schools start the day with yoga or a few minutes of quiet breathing. It helps both the body and the mind feel fresh.

games.title: Kind or unkind?
items: Sharing crayons with a friend
Calling someone names
Inviting a new child to play
Pushing in the line
Saying sorry after a mistake
Leaving someone out on purpose
Listening when a friend is sad

games.title: Feelings check
items: It is okay to feel angry sometimes.
Everyone feels angry at times. What matters is how we handle it.
We should keep all our worries a secret from everyone.
Talking to a trusted adult can help solve worries.
Teasing someone again and again is a kind of bullying.
Hurting someone with words again and again is bullying.
Taking deep breaths can help us calm down.
Slow breathing relaxes the body and mind.
If a touch feels unsafe, we should say 'No' and tell a trusted adult.
Our body belongs to us. Saying no and telling an adult keeps us safe.
Only grown-ups have feelings.
Children and adults all have feelings.

quiz.q: Which of these is a good way to calm down when you feel angry?
quiz.explain: Slow breathing helps the body relax so we can think clearly.
steps: When upset, take deep breaths or count to ten.
Answer: Take slow, deep breaths
quiz.mistake: Thinks letting anger out on others is fine

quiz.q: What is bullying?
options: Hurting someone again and again with words or actions
quiz.explain: Bullying is repeated hurting, teasing or leaving someone out on purpose.
steps: Bullying means hurting someone again and again with words or actions.
Answer: Hurting someone again and again with words or actions
quiz.mistake: Thinks only hitting counts as bullying

quiz.q: If someone is bullying you, what should you do?
options: Tell a teacher or a trusted adult
Stop coming to school without telling anyone
quiz.explain: A trusted adult can help stop the bullying. You do not have to handle it alone.
steps: Bullying is never okay.
Tell a teacher or a trusted adult.
Answer: Tell a teacher or a trusted adult
quiz.mistake: Thinks telling an adult is wrong

quiz.q: A new girl is sitting alone at playtime. What is the kind thing to do?
options: Invite her to join your game
quiz.explain: Including others helps them feel welcome.
steps: Being kind means including others in games.
Answer: Invite her to join your game
quiz.mistake: Does not think about how the new child feels

quiz.q: Who is a 'trusted adult'?
options: A grown-up you know well who keeps you safe, like a parent or teacher
Someone who asks you to keep secrets from your parents
quiz.explain: A trusted adult is someone who cares for you, like a parent, grandparent or teacher.
steps: A trusted adult is a grown-up you know well who keeps you safe.
Strangers and people online are not trusted adults.
Answer: A grown-up you know well who keeps you safe, like a parent or teacher
quiz.mistake: Thinks any grown-up can be trusted

quiz.q: Which of these helps keep our body and mind healthy?
options: Sitting with a phone all night
Playing, enough sleep and healthy food
quiz.explain: Exercise, sleep and good food keep us fit, fresh and in a good mood.
steps: Play, enough sleep and healthy food keep body and mind healthy.
Answer: Playing, enough sleep and healthy food
quiz.mistake: Does not link habits with feeling well

quiz.q: Meera feels nervous before her dance show. What can help her?
options: Talking to her teacher and taking deep breaths
quiz.explain: Sharing the feeling and breathing slowly can calm nervousness. Feeling nervous is normal.
steps: Feeling nervous is okay; talking about it helps.
Deep breaths help her calm down.
Answer: Talking to her teacher and taking deep breaths
quiz.mistake: Thinks nervous feelings should be hidden

quiz.q: Your friend made a mistake and feels bad. What can you say?
options: It's okay, everyone makes mistakes. Let's try again.
quiz.explain: Kind words help a friend feel better and try again.
steps: Kind words help a friend who feels bad.
Answer: It's okay, everyone makes mistakes. Let's try again.
quiz.mistake: Thinks making fun of mistakes is harmless

teach.ask: Gappu looks sad: 'A big bird laughs at my small wings every day. What should I do? How do we make school happy?'
teach.praise: Thank you! Being laughed at again and again is bullying, so I will tell my teacher. And I'll be kind to others too.
teach.nudge: What can I do if someone keeps hurting me? Who can I tell?

revise.summary: All feelings are okay, and talking helps. We calm down with deep breaths, are kind and include others, never bully, and tell a trusted adult about bullying or any uncomfortable touch.
focus: What bullying is and what to do
remember: Calm down: deep breaths, count to ten, talk to someone
Bullying = hurting someone again and again; tell a trusted adult
Uncomfortable touch: say 'No', move away, tell a trusted adult
traps: A stranger online is not a trusted adult.

learn.hook: Fire drills, earthquake drills, first aid boxes: schools practise safety so that everyone knows what to do if something goes wrong.
points: In an earthquake: Drop to the floor, take Cover under a strong desk, and Hold on until the shaking stops.
During a fire drill: stay calm, walk quickly in a line, do not run or push, use the stairs (never the lift), and go to the safe open ground.
For a small cut: wash it with clean water, cover it with a clean bandage, and tell an adult.
On the road: cross at a zebra crossing. Look right, then left, then right again. Red light means stop and green light means go.
In India, 112 is the one number to call for police, fire or ambulance help in an emergency.

example.q: The fire alarm rings during class. Two children want to run to the lift to get out quickly. Think it through: what should the class do?
steps: Lifts can stop working in a fire and trap people.
Running and pushing can make people fall.
So the class should line up, walk quickly down the stairs and go to the open ground.
example.answer: Walk calmly in a line, use the stairs, not the lift, and gather in the open ground.

learn.reallife: Find your school's first aid box and the fire extinguisher. Do you know where the assembly point is during a drill?

games.title: Fire drill steps
games.prompt: Put the fire drill steps in order
items: Hear the alarm and stop work
Stay calm and line up
Walk quickly down the stairs, no pushing
Reach the open assembly ground
Teacher counts everyone

items.q: Traffic light colour that means stop
Traffic light colour that means go
Striped place to cross the road
One emergency number for all help in India

quiz.q: What should you do first when an earthquake starts in class?
options: Drop, take cover under a strong desk and hold on
quiz.explain: Drop, Cover and Hold on protects your head and body from falling things.
steps: In an earthquake: Drop, take Cover under a strong desk, Hold on.
Answer: Drop, take cover under a strong desk and hold on
quiz.mistake: Thinks running out at once is safest

quiz.q: Why should we NOT use the lift during a fire?
options: It is too slow to be fun
It may stop working and trap people
quiz.explain: Fire can cut the electricity, so a lift may get stuck. Stairs are safer.
steps: During a fire, use the stairs, never the lift.
Electricity may fail and the lift may trap people.
Answer: It may stop working and trap people
quiz.mistake: Does not know lifts can fail in a fire

quiz.q: Which is the right way to cross a road?
options: Cross while looking at a phone
At the zebra crossing, after looking right, left and right again
Cross from behind a parked bus
quiz.explain: Zebra crossings are made for walkers, and looking both ways makes sure no vehicle is coming.
steps: Cross at a zebra crossing.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Answer: At the zebra crossing, after looking right, left and right again
quiz.mistake: Does not know safe road-crossing rules

quiz.q: Which number can you call in India for police, fire or ambulance help?
quiz.explain: 112 is India's single emergency number for all urgent help.
steps: In India, 112 is the one emergency number for police, fire or ambulance.
Answer: 112
quiz.mistake: Guesses a number from films or other countries

quiz.q: Aditi gets a small scrape on her knee while playing. What should be done first?
options: Wash it with clean water and cover it with a clean bandage
Ignore it and keep it dirty
Rub it with a dirty cloth
quiz.explain: Clean water washes away dirt and germs, and a bandage keeps the wound clean.
steps: For a small cut: wash with clean water, cover with a clean bandage, tell an adult.
Answer: Wash it with clean water and cover it with a clean bandage
quiz.mistake: Thinks home remedies like mud are safe for wounds

quiz.q: What does a yellow (amber) traffic light usually tell drivers?
quiz.explain: Amber means the light is about to change, so drivers should slow down and get ready to stop.
steps: Red means stop and green means go.
Amber means the light is about to change, so get ready to stop.
Answer: Get ready to stop
quiz.mistake: Thinks amber means hurry up

quiz.q: Why does a school hold fire drills and earthquake drills?
options: So everyone knows what to do and stays calm in a real emergency
quiz.explain: Practice helps us act quickly and safely without panic.
steps: Drills are practice.
They help everyone know what to do and stay calm in a real emergency.
Answer: So everyone knows what to do and stays calm in a real emergency
quiz.mistake: Does not see the point of practice

quiz.q: During a fire drill, the class should
options: run and push to be first
go back for their bags and toys
walk quickly in a line without pushing
quiz.explain: Walking in a line keeps everyone safe. Bags and toys can be left behind.
steps: In a fire drill: stay calm and walk quickly in a line, no running or pushing.
Answer: walk quickly in a line without pushing
quiz.mistake: Thinks being first is more important than being safe

teach.ask: Gappu hears a loud bell: 'Ring ring! Is that a fire drill? What do I do?'
teach.praise: Got it! Stay calm, walk in a line, take the stairs and wait in the open ground. I'm a drill expert now!
teach.nudge: Should I run or walk? And should I take the lift or the stairs?

revise.summary: For safety at school: Drop, Cover and Hold on in an earthquake; walk calmly in a line and use the stairs in a fire; clean and cover small cuts; cross roads at zebra crossings; call 112 in an emergency.
remember: Fire: stay calm, walk in a line, stairs not lift, go to open ground
Road: zebra crossing; look right, left, right; red stop, amber get ready, green go
traps: Never use the lift during a fire.
Don't go back for bags during a drill.
